outcome_variable_scope: The ratio (own - donor)/(own - 0.5) of accuracies against a third of each pair's human raters, per consensus bin, on r104's persisted records. No judge call, no new measurement, and no dependence on r104's noise model -- the attenuation factor cancels.
scope: NEITHER significant NOR equivalent at the pre-registered margin -- the interval covers zero and is wider than the margin, so this is an answerable-margin result and not a demonstration of invariance. Reports the share's ACROSS-BIN difference, not its level: the level inherits r104's single donor draw. Bins whose own-arm accuracy is within 0.05 of chance are refused rather than reported. The label is a third of each pair's raters, so accuracy levels are not comparable to r103's.
verdict: M ANSWERABLE MARGIN. Everything on this axis so far has been about the SIZE of the signal: r103 found attribution rising with human consensus, r104 established that 74% of that rise survives the label's own noise. None of it is about what the signal is MADE OF. The prompt-specific SHARE of over-chance accuracy -- (own - donor)/(own - 0.5), the fraction of everything the own rubric achieves above chance that its own prompt's criteria contribute -- runs 0.6948, 0.6991, 0.6840 across the same consensus bins, a span of 0.0151 against a pre-registered tolerance of 0.05, while the attribution it is a share OF rises +0.0853 to +0.2128, a +150% change. Bootstrap over PAIRS puts the high-minus-low share at -0.0101 [-0.1335,+0.1185]. SIGNIFICANCE AND EQUIVALENCE ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY, AND THIS IS NEITHER. The data do not SHOW a compositional shift -- the interval covers zero -- but they do not establish there is none either: the interval is 0.1260 wide at the half, against a pre-registered margin of 0.05, so a shift up to 0.1335 remains compatible with these records. Reading the 0.0151 point span as invariance would be a claim 8x larger than the measurement supports. What CAN be said: the composition does not move in step with the magnitude -- attribution rises +150% while the share's best estimate moves -0.0101 -- so the consensus gradient is not obviously a change in which normative layer does the work. Resolving it to the margin needs 24,959 pairs, 6.4x the 3,929 here (r91's budget: halving an interval costs 4x the units), and that is a preregistration number, not a result. THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS THE STRONGEST STATEMENT ON THIS AXIS: the attenuation factor CANCELS. Deattenuation divides both arms' over-chance accuracy by the same number, so the share computed from RAW accuracies equals the share computed from r104's DEATTENUATED ones -- verified to 2e-16, executed rather than asserted. This statistic needs no noise model, no independence assumption, and none of r104's confounds reach it. TWO-SIDED CONTROL: synthetic arms built with a CONSTANT share across bins read 0.0145 span; arms built with a share moving 0.30 to 0.70 read 0.4805. An instrument that reported invariance whatever the data could not report invariance, and this one recovers a planted shift. DENOMINATOR FLOOR: any bin whose own-arm accuracy is within 0.05 of chance is refused rather than printed -- that is exactly the failure that made r103's 2.95x over-chance ratio span unreadable, its lowest bin having a donor arm 0.0041 above chance. THE CONFOUND, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN: the donor arm is ONE draw (r88: sd 0.0055 pooled), and every bin inherits the SAME draw -- so a share difference ACROSS bins is not explained by which donors were sampled, though the share LEVEL is, and the level is not what this reports. SCOPE: computed on r104's persisted split records -- 47,148 records over 3,929 pairs of at least 12 raters, labelled by a THIRD of each pair's raters. The share is a ratio of two estimates from the same records, so the interval is a bootstrap over PAIRS rather than a symmetric standard error.
